note.question: How do many firms, hoping to detect efficacy and futility of the candidate drug early to save development costs, plan interim analyses of patient-response data in their clinical trials compare?
note.overview: The cost for developing a new drug ranged from $1 billion to more than $2 billion between 2010 and 2019. In addition to high development costs, the efficacy of the candidate drug, patient enrollment, the market exclusivity period (MEP), and the planning horizon are uncertain. Moreover, slow enrollment leads to increased costs, canceled clinical trials, and lost potential revenue.
